mechanism: Additive antiplatelet/anticoagulant effect increases bleeding risk.
recommended_action: Avoid combination unless specialist-directed; monitor INR and bleeding closely.

mechanism: NSAIDs increase GI bleeding risk and may displace warfarin protein binding.
recommended_action: Prefer alternative analgesic (e.g. paracetamol within limits); monitor INR if unavoidable.

mechanism: NSAID-related GI mucosal injury plus anticoagulation elevates bleeding risk.
recommended_action: Avoid; use non-NSAID analgesia if possible and seek clinician advice.

mechanism: Two NSAIDs together increase GI, renal, and cardiovascular adverse-effect risk without added benefit.
recommended_action: Use a single NSAID at the lowest effective dose; avoid stacking NSAIDs.

mechanism: Duplicate NSAID exposure increases adverse-effect risk.
recommended_action: Do not combine two NSAIDs; choose one agent.

mechanism: NSAID duplication increases GI and hepatic risk.
recommended_action: Avoid concurrent NSAIDs; review indication and duration.

mechanism: NSAIDs may reduce ACE-inhibitor antihypertensive effect and worsen renal function.
recommended_action: Limit NSAID duration; monitor BP, creatinine, and potassium.

mechanism: NSAID + ACE inhibitor can precipitate renal impairment, especially in volume depletion.
recommended_action: Avoid prolonged NSAID use; check renal function if co-prescribed.

mechanism: NSAID may blunt ACE-inhibitor effect and increase acute kidney injury risk.
recommended_action: Prefer short NSAID courses; monitor renal function and BP.

mechanism: Combined renal afferent/efferent effects raise AKI risk.
recommended_action: Avoid if possible; hydrate and monitor creatinine/potassium.

mechanism: NSAID + ARB can impair renal autoregulation and raise potassium.
recommended_action: Limit NSAID; monitor renal function and electrolytes.

mechanism: NSAID + ARB increases risk of renal adverse effects.
recommended_action: Avoid prolonged NSAID therapy; check creatinine.

mechanism: NSAID may reduce ARB efficacy and worsen kidney function.
recommended_action: Use lowest NSAID dose/shortest duration; monitor labs.

mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 activation of clopidogrel, potentially reducing antiplatelet effect.
recommended_action: Prefer a PPI with less CYP2C19 inhibition if gastroprotection is needed; seek clinician advice.

mechanism: Strong CYP2C19 inhibition may reduce clopidogrel activation.
recommended_action: Avoid combination when possible; discuss PPI choice with prescriber.

mechanism: Both affect serotonergic pathways; ondansetron may also reduce tramadol analgesic effect.
recommended_action: Monitor efficacy and serotonin-related symptoms; consider alternatives if needed.

mechanism: Dual renin–angiotensin–aldosterone blockade increases hyperkalemia and renal failure risk.
recommended_action: Monitor potassium and renal function closely; ensure indication is appropriate.

mechanism: ACE inhibitor + potassium-sparing diuretic raises hyperkalemia risk.
recommended_action: Check K+ and creatinine; avoid potassium supplements unless directed.

mechanism: NSAID increases bleeding risk with anticoagulants.
recommended_action: Avoid NSAID with warfarin when possible.

mechanism: Ibuprofen may interfere with aspirin's antiplatelet effect and increase GI bleeding risk.
recommended_action: If both needed, separate dosing per clinician advice; watch for GI symptoms.

mechanism: NSAID-related renal impairment can increase metformin accumulation and lactic acidosis risk.
recommended_action: Use NSAIDs cautiously; hold metformin if acute renal risk (sick day rules).

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce lithium clearance and can cause lithium toxicity.
recommended_action: Avoid NSAIDs or monitor lithium levels closely if unavoidable.

mechanism: NSAIDs can reduce methotrexate clearance and increase toxicity.
recommended_action: Avoid concurrent high-dose methotrexate with NSAIDs unless specialist-supervised.

mechanism: Fluoroquinolones may potentiate anticoagulant effect.
recommended_action: Monitor INR during and after antibiotic course.

mechanism: Macrolides may alter warfarin response in some patients.
recommended_action: Consider INR check if co-administered.

mechanism: Additive serotonergic effects increase serotonin syndrome and seizure risk.
recommended_action: Avoid combination when possible; monitor closely if used.

mechanism: SSRI + tramadol raises serotonin syndrome risk; CYP2D6 interactions may alter tramadol activation.
recommended_action: Prefer alternative analgesic; escalate if agitation, tremor, or hyperreflexia occur.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition markedly increases simvastatin exposure and myopathy risk.
recommended_action: Avoid combination; hold or switch statin per local guidance.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition can increase statin levels and muscle toxicity risk.
recommended_action: Consider temporary statin hold or dose review during macrolide course.

mechanism: Additive hyperkalemia risk with potassium-sparing diuretic plus potassium salts.
recommended_action: Avoid unsupervised potassium supplements; monitor serum K+.
